fields.acceptance: TestMakeTestTimeout runs make -n test and asserts: every go test line carries -trimpath, -timeout 20m and 9>&-; the packages other than cmd/rhiza start in the background before the lock; cmd/rhiza's scripts and then the timing budgets each run under a flock on a lock file beside GOCACHE, with a 'Waiting for another make test' line when it is held. Measured on the loaded 4-core VM: a fresh worktree of the same commit builds all 36 test binaries in 5 s with -trimpath against 143 s without (0 reused), and 22 of 35 internal packages are (cached) there; a second make test started while one holds the lock prints the waiting line and runs once it is free; where flock(1) is missing the suite runs unlocked; plan-workflow.txtar's fake rex answers block close, so the script takes 23 s instead of 509 s
fields.statement: make test is cheap to run from many worktrees on one machine: a second worktree at the same code reuses the first one's test builds and cached results, and only one worktree at a time runs cmd/rhiza's CPU-heavy scripts or the timing budgets, while the rest of the suite runs beside them

options: lock cmd/rhiza's scripts and the timing budgets, the rest unlocked beside them
lock the whole suite and the budget phase
fields.quote: "i think you should monitor the daemon and adjust accordingly. we likely have some performance issues to tackle." (owner, 2026-11-03/04)
fields.statement: make test builds with -trimpath and takes one machine-wide flock (beside GOCACHE) around cmd/rhiza's scripts and, separately, around the timing budgets; the other packages run unlocked in the background beside the scripts. Measured on the loaded 4-core VM (load 15-30): the non-script packages are latency-bound, not CPU-bound (internal/index, slice, gen and op three at once took 235 s against 407 s one after another, at the same 86 CPU-s each; internal/api spends 500-590 s of wall on far less CPU), so locking them would only queue waits; cmd/rhiza's scripts use about 430 CPU-s per run in parallel, so they are what thrashes
fields.wording: the owner's words; the design is the orchestrator's, as the owner's proxy
